doc.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

title: Dan Wall: a family of pianists and self-directed learning
summary: Wall grew up among professional pianists, took specialized study at Berklee, and learned mostly by listening and playing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Um hum. Did you guys come out of a music education background? Maybe you can address that first.

No, not so much with me. I was fortunate for one thing that I grew up in a family of professional piano players. It went back to my grandfather, my uncle is a very good pianist, my mom is still doing gigs, my two cousins, it’s kind of ridiculous. You know one is a record producer and a phenomenal reader. A well educated person as opposed to me. So I was at Berklee kind of doing just some specialized piano studies as opposed to really being involved in going after a degree and participating in ensembles, I was actually doing a lot of gigs around Boston and just, you know, at the school to kind of get what I felt that I needed to get. So I didn’t come out of the educational. Now I teach in colleges, which is kind of strange because I didn’t go through that system. I did most of my learning really from listening, from playing with people, and by having people in the family who I could actually sit down and listen to this great sound coming out of the piano with these great chord voicings, you know, and ask my uncle, what are you doing? And then I would sit down, I want to do that, I want to make this instrument sound this way too. So that was more of my education.
